subject: general
question: The Indian Prime Minister has launched a scheme named ______ on 11 October 2025 with a budgetary allocation of ₹11,440 crore for the period 2025-26 to 2030-31.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses** was launched by the **Indian Prime Minister** on **11 October 2025**.
 
• The mission is aimed at achieving **self-sufficiency in pulses production** during the **2025-26 to 2030-31** period.
 
• A total of **₹11,440 crore** has been allocated as the **budgetary provision** for this initiative.
 
• The mission focuses on **boosting domestic production** of pulses to reduce dependency on imports and ensure food security.
 
• This initiative aligns with the broader goal of the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan**, which emphasizes self-reliance in various sectors, including agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Pulses in India:**

 
 
• Pulses are a **vital source of protein** for a significant portion of the Indian population, especially vegetarians.
 
• India is the **largest producer, consumer, and importer** of pulses globally.
 
• The production of pulses plays a crucial role in addressing **malnutrition** and ensuring food security.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in **2020**, it aims to make India **self-reliant** in various sectors.
 
• The mission emphasizes **local production** to boost the economy and reduce reliance on imports.
 
• Agriculture is one of the **key focus areas** under this initiative.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Pulses:**
 
 
• The **National Food Security Mission (NFSM)** includes a specific component for increasing pulses production.
 
• Various subsidies and schemes are provided to **encourage farmers** to cultivate pulses.
 
• Minimum Support Prices (MSP) are regularly revised to ensure **fair prices** for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India imports a significant quantity of pulses from countries like **Canada, Myanmar, and Australia**.
 
• Enhancing domestic production will help **reduce import dependency** and save foreign exchange.
 
• The United Nations declared **2016** as the **International Year of Pulses** to highlight their importance in sustainable agriculture and food security.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pulses and Soil Health:**

 
 
• Pulses are known for their ability to **fix nitrogen** in the soil, improving soil fertility and reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
 
• Increased pulses cultivation contributes to **sustainable agricultural practices**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Pulses Production:**
 
 
• Erratic monsoons and **climate change** affect pulses yield significantly.
 
• Limited access to quality seeds and modern farming techniques among farmers.
 
• Price volatility and market uncertainties discourage farmers from cultivating pulses.
